title: The Human Statue Who Keeps Turning
premise: A busker freezes every time someone says the town's name, even when nobody is watching.
pressure: The busker's shoes have not moved, but his shadow has completed a full revolution. The crowd thinks the trick is magnificent; the performer looks ill.
investigate: Ask him to step outside the painted circle
success: His shadow bows alone and a chalk map beneath the paint reveals tomorrow's missing hour.
failure: He gets out, but his shadow remains under the crowd. The photographer saves a blurred image as evidence.
help: Offer the exhausted busker a chair and a break
helpOutcome: A stranger brings water. For once the applause is for the person, not the trick.

title: The Oyster That Won the Election
premise: A ballot kiosk announces an unopposed mollusk; only the losing candidate can hear its platform.
pressure: The oyster's manifesto proposes free shoreline access and quieter motors. The losing candidate wants the machine unplugged before anyone reads the fine print.
investigate: Get the defeated candidate to translate the shellfish platform
success: The supposed manifesto is a tidal forecast in legal language, including tomorrow's impossible low tide.
failure: The ballots blow into the fountain. The candidate admits the mollusk may understand the bay better than he does.
help: Invite the neighbors to an open debate
helpOutcome: Fishers and residents negotiate real access while the oyster listens in dignified silence.

title: The Man Selling Used Fog
premise: A persuasive stranger can bottle exactly one memory in a mason jar.
pressure: A seller's jars are labeled FIRST KISS, LAST BUS and THINGS LEFT UNSAID. One contains a street you almost remember walking, on a night you never lived.
investigate: Locate the original owner of the memory
success: She recognizes a bus route planned for ten years from now, right down to its unbuilt terminal.
failure: The lid cracks and the memory becomes wet-paper scent; you retain the name of a street.
help: Insist the bottled memories go back to their owners
helpOutcome: Three strangers recover enough of themselves to call someone they have missed.

title: Plaza Clock, Wrong County
premise: The clock strikes thirteen; everyone else insists it always has.
pressure: On the thirteenth chime, shops hang CLOSED FOR THE OTHER COUNTY signs. A delivery driver is stranded between maps that disagree on the street.
investigate: Compare the clock against bus and store records
success: Four independent clocks lost the same minute. A detour points to a street beneath the bay.
failure: Your watch stops and restarts; you still record which shop changed first.
help: Help the driver save the food
helpOutcome: Neighbors improvise a shared refrigerator rather than leave the vegetables to time.

title: Audience of One Hundred and One
premise: A midnight screening has one more shadow than ticket holders.
pressure: Every ticket is accounted for, but one silhouette keeps arriving late and taking a different seat. It carries a coat none of the patrons remembers.
investigate: Trace the shadow through the aisle lights
success: The phantom's reserved seat appears on a ticket dated next week.
failure: The lights flicker and you lose it, but the usher agrees to witness another screening.
help: Offer the uncounted guest its own seat
helpOutcome: It sits beside the exit and applauds the film everyone else forgets to watch.

title: Rocky Horror, Actual Horror
premise: A shadow-cast prop gains agency and demands better stage directions.
pressure: The shadow cast's alien prop refuses to be stabbed on cue and demands a speaking part. The director threatens to cancel the fundraiser.
investigate: Rewrite the prop's scene in front of the cast
success: Its unscripted speech includes the address of a warehouse that will appear tomorrow.
failure: The crowd boos, but a penciled stage direction in the old script was written by nobody present.
help: Help the troupe replace an unsafe stunt
helpOutcome: The actors invent a safer gag; the prop returns to its rack under its own power.

title: Simplex's Encore
premise: A phantom theater cat walks through the projection beam and selects tomorrow's film.
pressure: A cat-shaped gap in the projection selects a film about a theater fire decades ago. The film ends tomorrow, with a weather warning.
investigate: Follow the phantom cat into the booth
success: Inside the canister you find a program printed for tomorrow and a warning about the harbor.
failure: The projectionist interrupts, but you both see a paw print on the glass from the inside.
help: Ask the theater staff to make copies
helpOutcome: They preserve the reel before morning, and no one has to steal the evidence.

title: The Film That Watches Back
premise: A lost reel depicts the player's next choice, badly subtitled.
pressure: A lost film plays the choice you are about to make, accompanied by subtitles that misrepresent your motives. The actor on screen looks ashamed.
investigate: Inspect individual frames before making your decision
success: Three frames show a compassionate third choice and a sign pointing to Trinidad.
failure: The reel snaps at its most useful moment; you retain a strip showing an impossible street.
help: Ask the audience to invent another ending
helpOutcome: The debate is messy and kind. When the film resumes, the actor finally looks relieved.

title: The Trail with Two Trailheads
premise: A jogger repeatedly emerges at the trailhead they have not reached.
pressure: A jogger emerges at the wrong trailhead twice. His watch records uphill miles while both maps insist he ran downhill.
investigate: Mark each junction and walk the loop backward
success: One trail marker ages fifty years between passes. Distance is not the thing being rearranged.
failure: You return to the start empty-handed but find a second set of fresh footprints beside yours.
help: Guide the frightened jogger out before nightfall
helpOutcome: A volunteer search team meets you at the gate, ready to help the next lost walker.

title: The Deer in the Reflective Vest
premise: A park volunteer gives safety instructions for events scheduled in 1897.
pressure: A deer in reflective gear hands you a warning from 1897. The old notice describes a collapsed bridge under today's heavily used trail.
investigate: Inspect the bank before dismissing the warning
success: The soil is unstable in exactly the place the impossible notice names.
failure: The deer vanishes before you read the seal, but the ground slumps under your boot.
help: Help volunteers close the risky section
helpOutcome: Hikers take a marked detour. The deer waits until the last child is clear.

title: Mushroom Neighborhood Watch
premise: A fungus network files very specific complaints about the living.
pressure: Mushrooms have written an unusually detailed noise complaint about a drainage pipe that nobody admits installing.
investigate: Turn the complaint into a site survey
success: You uncover a buried pipe with a future-dated invoice and diverted water.
failure: Rain ruins your measurements, but the displaced soil remains obvious.
help: Call the trail crew and include the neighbors
helpOutcome: The crew restores the water without trampling the colony, though the mushrooms file an appeal.

title: Campfire Without a Camp
premise: Invisible campers gossip about the player's future over cold ash.
pressure: An empty ring of chairs encircles cold ash. Invisible campers argue about whether you will betray someone whose name you have not heard.
investigate: Ask the unseen speakers to name the missing person
success: The name appears in ash beside a date that has not happened.
failure: They answer only with an old song; an unworn boot leaves a fresh print.
help: Leave the site safer than you found it
helpOutcome: An unseen voice thanks you for clearing the ring rather than exploiting the mystery.

title: Office Hours with a Visiting Moon
premise: A lecturer's guest speaker insists it is the actual moon on sabbatical.
pressure: The visiting moon occupies a tiny campus lectern while daylight crosses the windows. The professor introduces it without irony.
investigate: Ask which coastline the moon remembers
success: Its crater chart illuminates a harbor with two lighthouses, only one of them built.
failure: The answer comes as a moving tide line on the blackboard, and students record it.
help: Let skeptical students ask their own questions
helpOutcome: The lecture becomes a serious public seminar where uncertainty is welcome.

title: Dorm Room 404
premise: A missing dorm room has a remarkably active meal plan.
pressure: Dorm 404 does not exist, yet someone leaves shoes at the wall and the cafeteria charges three meals a day to its resident.
success: The swipe belongs to a student enrolled next autumn. Their listed emergency contact is the building.
failure: The registrar closes the card but a hot dinner appears beside the blank wall.
helpOutcome: Housing staff leave a note and a safe way to answer. The response says THANK YOU FOR KNOCKING.

title: The Thesis Defense of the Dead
premise: An academic committee includes someone who never graduated and never died.
pressure: The fourth member of a thesis committee has never lived or died. She gives devastatingly precise feedback on a dissertation still being written.
investigate: Check the minutes of earlier defenses
success: A correction in her handwriting identifies a historical error the faculty has not yet committed.
failure: Her signature fades from the minutes. The candidate keeps the useful argument.
help: Protect the student's right to a fair defense
helpOutcome: The impossible examiner drops an unreasonable demand and asks a genuine question.

title: The Mascot Disputes Biology
premise: The campus mascot begins providing accurate but unwanted zoological advice.
pressure: The mascot stops cheering to give zoological advice about animals absent from the north coast. The field notes are uncomfortably accurate.
investigate: Compare the drawings with the campus collection
success: A species declared extinct is visible in a field sketch made yesterday at the marsh.
failure: The zipper jams before you can copy the notes. You still recognize the wing pattern.
help: Make sure the sweating performer gets a break
helpOutcome: A stagehand brings water, and the mascot returns to being a person.

title: Finals Week from Another Timeline
premise: Exams arrive before classes and the university refuses refunds.
pressure: Students receive final exams before their first lecture. The questions are about public decisions the town has not yet made.
investigate: Audit an exam against the course plan
success: One answer predicts a flood-barrier dispute fifteen years hence, including an unfamiliar civic seal.
failure: The registrar keeps the paper, but you remember the date and the name of a proposed creek.
help: Set up a study group to compare evidence
helpOutcome: Students share food and notes instead of competing for grades awarded before learning.
